arxiv.title: KiRA: Kronecker Input-Gated Rank Adaptation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Pretrained Models
arxiv.star_quote: the update $\Delta W$ is the Kronecker product of a frozen random $p\times p$ matrix $A$ and a trainable factor $M(x)$, which overcomes the rank ceiling
arxiv.headline: Kronecker積を用いた低ランク制約を超越する高効率パラメータ微調整手法KiRA
arxiv.what: 学習済みモデルの微調整において、低ランク行列の積の代わりに、固定されたランダム行列と学習可能な因子のKronecker積を用いる手法です。入力ゲートg(x)により、入力サンプルごとに適応的なランク調整を動的に行います。
arxiv.enables: LoRAと比較して学習パラメータ数を8.7〜9.7倍削減しながら、6つの医療画像・言語ベンチマークで最高スコアを達成しました。
arxiv.why_it_matters: 従来のPEFT手法における「低ランクの天井」を打破し、タスクごとに最適な表現能力を少ないパラメータで提供できるため、エッジデバイス等での効率的な展開に寄与します。

arxiv.title: Fast and Scalable Abstract Interpretation for Deep Neural Networks
arxiv.star_quote: Scepter handles networks with up to 153x as many neurons as the largest completed by the corresponding baselines.
arxiv.headline: 構造セマンティクスによる深層ニューラルネットワークの高速・スケーラブルな抽象解釈フレームワーク
arxiv.what: 中間抽象値の構造を決定し、数値評価を遅延させる構造セマンティクスを用いることで、抽象解釈器を特化させるScepterを提案しています。これにより、連続する操作の計算を統合し、実行可能なテンソルプログラムを生成します。
arxiv.enables: 既存手法と比較して、最大153倍の規模のニューロンを持つネットワークを処理でき、ResNet50やVGG-16でのDeepPoly解析を完遂しました。GPU上での幾何平均速度向上は11.9倍から44.4倍に達し、ピークメモリも平均2.6倍削減されます。
arxiv.why_it_matters: これまで計算コストの高さから小規模モデルに限定されていた厳密な安全性・特性検証を、大規模な実用モデルに適用可能にします。

arxiv.title: Casper: A Projection-Based Neurosymbolic Layer for Scalable & Guaranteed Constraint Satisfaction
arxiv.star_quote: Casper casts constraint satisfaction as a closed-form Euclidean projection onto the constraint-feasible region, computable in a single forward pass.
arxiv.headline: ユークリッド射影により制約の100%遵守を保証する神経記号論的レイヤーCasper
arxiv.what: 制約充足を制約可能領域への閉形式のユークリッド射影として定式化した、微分可能かつ自動化された神経記号論的レイヤーです。推論時に1回のフォワードパスで計算可能であり、既存のあらゆるニューラル予測器と組み合わせることができます。
arxiv.enables: Warcraftの経路探索（30x30グリッド）において、既存手法がタイムアウトや低い有効率（7%未満）に留まる中、100%の有効なパス生成を大規模に実現しました。
arxiv.why_it_matters: 制約の厳密な遵守が求められる実世界のタスクに対し、近似ではなく保証を伴う解を、推論速度を犠牲にせずに提供します。

arxiv.title: Flipping the Coins: Training Physical Simulators through Hard Switches
arxiv.star_quote: we introduce EventFlip, which flips a near-threshold switch from a stored state, replays the original solver, and measures the loss difference
arxiv.headline: ハードスイッチを含む物理シミュレータの偏りのない勾配学習を実現するEventFlip
arxiv.what: 物理エンジンの不連続な挙動（ハードスイッチ）に対し、スイッチの切り替え前後での差分を測定し、連続的なパス勾配とジャンプ項を組み合わせた不偏勾配推定量を提供します。閾値に微小なガウスノイズを加え、確率的な二値決定としてモデル化します。
arxiv.enables: 電力網の連鎖解裂や爆轟波のシミュレーションにおいて、最強のベースラインと比較して誤差を1.4〜1.5倍削減し、すべてのタスクで最小エラーを記録しました。
arxiv.why_it_matters: 物理法則に基づくハイブリッドシミュレータの学習において、自動微分が扱えなかった不連続な事象の最適化を正確に行えるようになります。
tags: 物理シミュレーション

arxiv.title: MolGPAO: Molecular Generative Pre-trained Autoregressive Octree with Speculative Decoding and Sub-Millisecond Seam Healing for 3D Molecules
arxiv.star_quote: MolGPAO lifts drug-scale valid-connected yield 6.78x (12.7% to 86.2%, 99.83% atom stability), runs 7.3x faster (or 1.65x faster at 2.0x yield) than 100-step FlowMol
arxiv.headline: 3D分子生成における原子安定性と推論速度を両立する自己回帰型八分木モデルMolGPAO
arxiv.what: 3D八分木（Octree）を用いた自己回帰生成に、スペック解析デコーディングとMortonシームの修復技術を導入したアーキテクチャです。共有の批判モデル（Critic）とSE(3)不変なリファイナーを統合し、幾何学的平衡と原子価の安定性を確保します。
arxiv.enables: GEOM-Drugs等のデータセットで、有効な結合を持つ分子の生成率を6.78倍（12.7%から86.2%へ）向上させ、FlowMolに対し7.3倍の高速化を達成しました。
arxiv.why_it_matters: 拡散モデルやフローモデルといった計算負荷の高い手法に代わり、大規模な創薬ターゲット分子を高速かつ正確に生成する実用的な手段を提供します。

arxiv.title: Improving Tail-Augmented Speculative Drafting with Hidden State Mixing and Gradient Detach
arxiv.star_quote: Hidden State Mixing (HSM) samples among backbone and MTP hidden states aligned to the same prediction target, exposing the drafter to mixtures of states
arxiv.headline: 隠れ状態の混合と勾配切断によりスペック解析デコーディングの受容率を向上させる学習手法
arxiv.what: マルチトークン予測（MTP）モジュールの学習において、バックボーンとMTPの隠れ状態をサンプリングして混合するHidden State Mixing（HSM）と、特定のパスの勾配を遮断するHidden State Gradient Detach（HSGD）を提案しています。推論コストを増やさずに、学習と推論の不一致を解消します。
arxiv.enables: Qwen3やDeepSeek-V4-Pro等において、平均受容長を最大52.2%改善し、既存のEAGLE-3と比較して学習時のピークメモリを48%削減しました。
arxiv.why_it_matters: LLMの推論加速に不可欠なスペック解析デコーディングの効率を、追加のハードウェアリソースなしで向上させることができます。
tags: スペック解析デコーディング

arxiv.title: Counting Beyond Frames: Codec Motion Tells Frozen Diffusion VLMs How Many
arxiv.star_quote: We are the first to show that this motion provides direct evidence for the count: a candidate count is a testable motion hypothesis
arxiv.headline: ビデオコーデックの動き情報を活用しVLMの計数能力を劇的に向上させるCoDiCount
arxiv.what: ビデオコーデックが記録しているブロック置換（動きベクトル）を直接的な証拠として利用し、計数タスクを解決する学習不要のフレームワークです。拡散ベースのVision-Language Model（dVLM）のデノイジング過程において、計数メッセージを用いて確率を再重み付けします。
arxiv.enables: 7Bのモデルでありながら、MotionBenchにおいてGPT-5.1やGemini-2.5-Proを凌駕し、TOMATOベンチマークでGPT-4oを上回る精度を達成しました。
arxiv.why_it_matters: VLMが苦手とする「動的な事象の計数」に対し、追加学習なしで、既存の圧縮ビデオデータが持つ情報を活用する効率的なアプローチを提示しています。

arxiv.title: Collect for Coverage, Replay with Evidence: Adaptive and Efficient On-Policy Distillation for Long-Horizon Agents
arxiv.star_quote: On SWE-bench Verified, it raises task success to 59.5%
arxiv.headline: 証拠に基づくリプレイと学生主導の収集による長期間エージェントの効率的・適応的な方策蒸留
arxiv.what: 長期間（Long-horizon）タスクにおいて、現在の学生モデルから生成した履歴に教師モデルが補完を行う「学生シード型収集」と、実行結果の証拠に基づいて重要なターンを選択する「後知恵リプレイ割り当て」を組み合わせたCARE-OPDを提案しています。
arxiv.enables: SWE-bench Verifiedにおいて、タスク成功率を59.5%まで高めつつ、従来のオンライン方策蒸留と比較して学習時間を45%、環境アクション数を44%削減しました。
arxiv.why_it_matters: ソフトウェアエンジニアリング等の複雑なタスクにおいて、高コストな環境インタラクションを最小限に抑えつつ、効率的にエージェントを強化できます。

arxiv.title: DFly2: Turbocharging Long-Context Speculative Decoding by Sharing the Target's Sparsity
arxiv.star_quote: Its throughput is 62% and 81% higher on two 64K sets.
arxiv.headline: ターゲットモデルのスパース構造を共有しロングコンテキスト推論を高速化するDFly2
arxiv.what: ターゲットモデル（DeepSeek-V4等）が持つスパースアテンションのKVキャッシュと選択されたインデックスをドラフトモデルがそのまま共有する、スペック解析デコーディング手法です。ドラフトモデル独自のキャッシュ保持やスコアリングパスを不要にします。
arxiv.enables: ロングコンテキストやエージェント関連のワークロードにおいて、既存手法に対し受容率を10.0%〜31.5%向上させ、DS-V4.1-Flashでのスループットを最大81%改善しました。
arxiv.why_it_matters: スパースな大規模モデルにおけるメモリ帯域と計算のボトルネックを解消し、長大なコンテキストでのリアルタイム推論を現実的なものにします。
tags: スパースアテンション

arxiv.title: ProbFaS: Probabilistic Video Frame Selection for MLLMs via Multi-Fidelity Calibration
arxiv.star_quote: ProbFaS is the most accurate among fourteen state-of-the-art training-free selectors
arxiv.headline: マルチフィデリティ・ガウス過程による長尺動画の重要なフレームを特定するProbFaS
arxiv.what: 低コストだがバイアスのある画像・テキスト整合性（ITA）スコアと、高コストだが正確なMLLMの判断をコ・クリギング（多忠実度ガウス過程）で統合し、最適なフレームを選択する確率的パイプラインです。MLLMの内部的なYes/No判断を校正信号として利用します。
arxiv.enables: Video-MME等の主要ベンチマークにおいて、32フレームの選択で既存の128フレーム選択や768フレームの均等サンプリングを上回る精度を達成しました。
arxiv.why_it_matters: 計算リソースが限られるMLLMにおいて、情報を損失することなく入力トークン数を劇的に削減できるため、長尺動画理解の実用性が高まります。

arxiv.title: LiveVAE: Causal Window Attention Makes Efficient Streaming Video VAE
arxiv.star_quote: LiveVAE achieves 5.2-6.2x faster encoding and 3.0-3.3x faster decoding
arxiv.headline: 因果ウィンドウアテンションによりストリーミング対応の高速ビデオVAEを実現するLiveVAE
arxiv.what: ビデオVAEの符号化・復号化において、局所的な時空間近傍のみに依存する因果ウィンドウアテンションを採用したアーキテクチャです。事前学習済みVAEの潜在空間を維持するための蒸留と微調整を経て、ドロップインで置き換え可能なモジュールとして構築されます。
arxiv.enables: 公式のVAEと比較して、符号化で5.2〜6.2倍、復号化で3.0〜3.3倍の高速化を達成し、専用インフラとの組み合わせで最大13.4倍の高速化を実現しました。
arxiv.why_it_matters: ビデオ生成・編集パイプラインにおける主要な遅延要因であったVAEを、メモリ効率の高いストリーミング処理可能にすることで、インタラクティブな用途への道を拓きます。

arxiv.title: SpiderSkel: Sub-Pixel Multi-Tangent 2D Skeletonization from Inscribed-Disc Geometry
arxiv.comment: 13 pages, 4 figures, 5 tables, plus 6 pages of supplementary material. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Image Processing
arxiv.star_quote: every variant is Pareto-optimal with respect to all twenty-two baselines
arxiv.headline: 内接円幾何に基づき位相と再構成精度を保証するサブピクセル2Dスケルトン化手法SpiderSkel
arxiv.what: バイナリ形状をコンパクトな内側表現（スケルトン）に変換する手法で、正確なユークリッド距離変換と内接円の接点配置を利用してサブピクセル位置を特定します。成分や穴のトポロジー維持を理論的に保証し、接続性を確保したまま削減を行います。
arxiv.enables: 11,000枚以上の画像ベンチマークにおいて、22の既存手法を上回る再構成精度（Dice係数）と削減率を達成しました。また、エディット後の再計算を平均15.4〜18.1msで完了する高速性を持ちます。
arxiv.why_it_matters: 医療画像やインフラ診断における微細な形状解析において、解像度の損失なしに数学的に正しい構造抽出が可能になります。

arxiv.title: KnitNet: Learning to Search at Inference Time for Exact RNA Inverse Design
arxiv.star_quote: KnitNet is the first method to achieve exact computational matches for all complex, pseudoknotted structures.
arxiv.headline: フィードバック学習による検索で正確なRNA逆設計を実現するKnitNet
arxiv.what: 特定の構造に折り畳まれるRNA塩基配列を探索する際、検証器（Verifier）からのフィードバックを用いてシーケンスを洗練させる推論時スケーリングフレームワークです。ミスマッチした構造から塩基間の依存関係を推論し、修正戦略を動的に適応させます。
arxiv.enables: 5つの主要ベンチマークにおいて、従来のサンプリング手法より70%少ない時間で解の発見率を平均21ポイント向上させ、OpenKnot57の複雑な疑似ノット構造すべてで正確な一致を達成しました。
arxiv.why_it_matters: 学習済み生成モデルの限界を超え、推論時の計算量を増やすことでより困難なRNA設計問題を解決する「推論時スケーリング」の有効性を示しています。
tags: バイオインフォマティクス

arxiv.title: Beat This! Live - Online Beat and Downbeat Tracking by Predicting the Future
arxiv.comment: Accepted at the 27th International Society for Music Information Retrieval Conference (ISMIR), 2026
arxiv.star_quote: F1-score improves from 80.6 to 86.7 for beats and 56.5 to 74.1 for downbeats
arxiv.headline: 未来予測により低遅延かつ高精度なリアルタイムビート追跡を実現するBeat This! Live
arxiv.what: 最新のオフラインビート追跡モデルをリアルタイム・ストリーミング向けに因果（Causal）化したモデルです。時間的にシフトさせたラベルを用いて学習することで、現在のフレームよりわずかに先の予測を行い、レイテンシ削減とピーク検出の精度向上を両立させています。
arxiv.enables: GTZANデータセットにおいて、既存のSOTAであるBeatNet+と比較し、ビートのF1スコアを80.6から86.7へ、ダウンビートを56.5から74.1へと大幅に向上させました。
arxiv.why_it_matters: 音楽のライブ演奏やDJプレイ等のリアルタイム性が要求される現場において、プロレベルの精度でビート同期を可能にします。

arxiv.title: Lightweight Reasoning Transfer via Chain-of-Thought Vector Projection
arxiv.star_quote: We study projected cross-model Chain-of-Thought (CoT) Vector transfer, a two-stage approach that keeps both models frozen.
arxiv.headline: 軽量な線形プロジェクタによる大規模モデルから小規模モデルへの思考連鎖（CoT）能力の転送
arxiv.what: 教師モデルから抽出したCoTベクトル（推論タスクの特性を捉えたベクトル）を、線形プロジェクタを介して凍結された学生モデルの残差空間に注入する手法です。学生モデルの学習には教師の出力や中間トレースを必要とせず、少量の最終回答ラベルのみを使用します。
arxiv.enables: GSM8KやMATHベンチマークにおいて、学生モデルの精度を10.37〜21.98ポイント向上させ、コード生成においてもQwen2.5-7Bの性能を有意に引き上げました。
arxiv.why_it_matters: モデルを凍結したまま、極めて軽量な適応レイヤーを追加するだけで、小規模モデルに高度な推論能力を付与できる実用的な手段となります。

arxiv.title: Escapingthe instruction blackhole of vision-language-action policies via optimal-transport wormholes
arxiv.star_quote: We propose Wormhole, a training-free plug-in that relocates the robot instead of re-instructing it: optimal transport selects an approach-phase state of the new task
arxiv.headline: 指示変更への追従不能問題を「ワームホール」転送で解決するロボット制御手法Wormhole
arxiv.what: VLA（視覚・言語・行動）ポリシーが一度特定のタスクを開始すると新しい指示を無視する現象（指示ブラックホール）を解決するため、ロボットの状態を新タスクの開始フェーズに最適な輸送（Optimal Transport）を用いて再配置する、学習不要のプラグインです。
arxiv.enables: LIBEROベンチマークにおいて、タスク実行中の指示変更による成功率を1.2%以下から93.1%へと劇的に改善しました。
arxiv.why_it_matters: 人間との協調において不可欠な「途中で指示を変える」という柔軟性を、ポリシーの再学習なしで既存のロボット制御系に付与できます。

arxiv.title: When Every Rollout Fails: Splicing Learner-Conditioned Options into Long-Horizon Agent RL
arxiv.star_quote: We introduce SPLICE, which constructs local training targets from failed current-policy trajectories online.
arxiv.headline: 報酬ゼロの失敗軌道から学習ターゲットを合成する長期間エージェント強化手法SPLICE
arxiv.what: すべてのサンプリング結果が失敗（報酬ゼロ）となる困難なタスクにおいて、失敗した軌道から適切なスライスポイントを選び、プロポーザルモデルを用いて部分的な解（オプション）を合成・注入する手法です。その後の成功確率を推定し、価値の高い遷移を学習ターゲットとして利用します。
arxiv.enables: SWE-bench VerifiedやDeep Researchタスクにおいて、標準的なGRPO手法を2.8〜9.8ポイント上回り、元々失敗していた課題のクリア率を10.8ポイント向上させました。
arxiv.why_it_matters: 報酬が極めて疎な長期間タスクにおいて、外部の完全な正解データに頼りすぎることなく、自己改善ループを回すことが可能になります。

arxiv.title: Real2SimLab: A Unified Platform for Real-to-Simulation Transfer
arxiv.headline: 現実世界の映像からシミュレーションを構築するReal-to-Sim研究の統合プラットフォーム
arxiv.what: ビデオ録画からシミュレーションプログラムを生成するエージェントを評価・学習するための統一プラットフォームです。異なるベンチマーク間の入出力とスコアリングを統合し、データ汚染を排除した学習データ生成パイプラインを提供します。
arxiv.enables: 現在47のコーディングエージェントと6つのベンチマークをサポートし、300本近い論文をまとめたリサーチマップも提供しています。
arxiv.why_it_matters: バラバラだったReal-to-Sim評価指標を共通化することで、ロボティクスやデジタルツイン分野の開発効率を向上させます。

arxiv.title: Sage-Med: Scaling Medical Multimodal Intelligence
arxiv.headline: 322M件の記録と段階的学習による医療用マルチモーダルLLM、Sage-Med
arxiv.what: 3億件を超える医療データを用いた事前学習、段階的な教師あり微調整、適応的強化学習を組み合わせた35Bパラメータ（3Bアクティブ）の混合専門家（MoE）モデルです。視覚的知覚と医療言語能力を同時にスケールさせるカリキュラムを導入しています。
arxiv.enables: 31の公開ベンチマークで平均58.26%を記録し、既存のSOTAであるHulu-Med-235BやIntern-S2-Previewを上回り、GPT-6.2-Sol等のプロプライエタリモデルに迫る性能を示しました。
arxiv.why_it_matters: 医療分野におけるMLLMのスケーリング則を検証し、臨床ワークフローや複雑な診断推論に向けた具体的な学習レシピとベンチマークを提示しています。

arxiv.title: Mixture-of-Loops Transformer
arxiv.headline: 層の再利用とメモリ機構により効率と表現力を両立するMixture-of-Loops Transformer
arxiv.what: トランスフォーマーの層をループ（再利用）させるアーキテクチャに、層間やループ間でKVキャッシュを選択的に記憶・再利用するMoLA（Mixture-of-Loops Attention）を導入したモデルです。効率重視のMoLT-KVと表現力重視のMoLT-Rの2つのバリエーションがあります。
arxiv.enables: 400Bトークンの事前学習において、OLMo3に対し700Mモデルで1.7倍のトークン効率を達成し、3B MoEモデルでも10のドメインでPerplexityと精度を改善しました。
arxiv.why_it_matters: モデルサイズを抑えつつ、深層モデルに匹敵する表現力を獲得できるため、推論効率と精度のトレードオフを改善する新しい設計指針となります。

arxiv.title: Stable Gated DeltaNet-2: Understanding and Mitigating Recurrent State Instability
arxiv.headline: 対称的な消去機構により再帰状態の不安定性を解消したStable Gated DeltaNet-2
arxiv.what: 線形アテンションベースのモデルGDN-2における、ロングコンテキスト学習時の不安定性を理論的に解析し修正したモデルです。書き換え操作における非正規な演算子が引き起こす指数的増大を防ぐため、対称的な消去（Symmetric Erasure）と減衰調整された残差書き込みを採用しました。

arxiv.title: Improving and Expanding Video Editing Capabilities Without Videos

hf.title: Motion Mamba 2.0: Autoregressive Diffusion Mamba for Long-Horizon Humanoid Control
hf.abstract: Long-horizon, real-time controllable motion generation is essential for interactive animation and humanoid robotics, where an agent must respond to changing instructions and spatial goals while moving. Existing autoregressive diffusion methods generate motion incrementally, but bounded attention caches limit access to distant history, while repeated denoising introduces substantial inference overhead. We present Motion Mamba 2.0, a Mamba-based root-body diffusion architecture that integrates local attention, resumable recurrent states, and persistent content memory (PCM) for long-horizon controllable motion generation. PCM transforms compressed motion history from Mamba recurrent states, together with state changes and text-conditioned features, into dynamically updated content slots accessible to local attention. To enable efficient inference, we further develop an execution scheme tailored to this architecture, combining CUDA Graph replay, fused kernels, and execution-flow simplification while preserving the canonical history update. Evaluations on retargeted HiPHI demonstrate accurate terminal control over rollouts of up to 39.52 s, while short-horizon comparisons on BONES Seed and retargeted HumanML3D show that the model also retains strong spatial control and text-motion matching. On an RTX 4090, the optimized execution reduces median complete-window latency from 1685.35 to 276.14 ms, achieving a median paired speedup of 6.138times while preserving identical outputs and committed states in the tested rollouts. Moreover, we conduct extensive real-world evaluation on the Unitree G1, demonstrating sequential text-guided action composition, expressive motion, and interactive locomotion through keyboard and mouse control.

hf.summary_ja: 局所アテンションと永続コンテンツメモリを統合し、低遅延かつ長期的な動作生成を実現。

hf.title: WorldLeague: Benchmarking Physical Agency
hf.abstract: AI systems can now operate Blender, follow instructions in complex video games, and manipulate objects with robot arms. What range of physical goals can today's AI systems achieve autonomously? Answering this question requires testing systems on tasks that demand different combinations of perception, memory, planning, and action. We introduce WorldLeague, a benchmark that compares AI systems on a common set of 60 simulated robot tasks by measuring progress toward each task's physical goal from the robot's trajectory. Robots explore scenes to gather evidence in WorldSeek, rearrange objects in WorldShape, and adapt to changes in WorldShift. Tying these goals to a single control interface limits which AI systems can be compared. In WorldLeague, vision-language models (VLMs) choose targets and motions, while vision-language-action models (VLAs) and world-action models (WAMs) use their native controls. For each of six capability dimensions, we measure how much progress a system makes toward its goals (Interactive Score) and how often it achieves them (physical success rate). Together, these measures form the system's Physical Agency Profile. Among 13 representative AI systems, Claude Fable 5.2 achieves 13 of the 60 goals and earns the highest mean Interactive Score (28.58/100). Fable leads in four dimensions, while GPT-6.1-Sol and GPT-6-Astra tie for first on rule-following tasks. Even when VLMs answer every final question correctly, they receive an Interactive Score of zero in 71.8\% of those episodes. WorldLeague gives Embodied AI, Physical AI, and Agentic AI a shared basis for comparing what AI systems achieve autonomously, from partial progress toward a physical goal to full goal completion. Project Webpage: https://xyangzhou.github.io/WorldLeague
hf.title_ja: WorldLeague: 物理的エージェンシーのベンチマーク
hf.summary_ja: 知覚・計画・行動が必要な60のシミュレーション任務を通じAIの物理的能力を測定する。

hf.title: Real2SimLab: A Unified Platform for Real-to-Simulation Transfer
hf.abstract: Real-to-simulation transfer, which builds simulations from real-world observations, has long been studied in research and industry. Recently, coding agents have become capable of generating simulation programs from video recordings, and several benchmarks have been proposed to evaluate them. However, each individual benchmark defines its own inputs, deliverables, and scoring pipeline. This leads to N times M integrations when evaluating N methods on M benchmarks. To this end, we present Real2SimLab, a unified platform for real-to-simulation transfer. It evaluates a method by running its written program and scoring the output simulation with the original scorer of each benchmark. Moreover, Real2SimLab provides a pipeline to create training data and reward annotations for real-to-simulation methods. Our pipeline carefully avoids data contamination by filtering out the video recordings that exist in benchmarks. For each video recording, a program is first produced, and then our pipeline computes its reward with the same code that Real2SimLab uses for evaluation. So far, it supports 47 coding agents and 5 non-agent methods on 6 benchmarks. Both the platform and Awesome-Real2Sim, our research map of nearly 300 real-to-simulation papers, are open source, and we invite the Real2SimHub community to build them together.
hf.title_ja: Real2SimLab: 実世界からシミュレーションへの移行のための統合プラットフォーム
hf.summary_ja: 異なるベンチマークの入力と評価を統一し、シミュレーション生成手法を効率的に比較。

hf.title: Antom 3-in-1 Transformer: A Payment Foundation Model
hf.abstract: We report the development of Antom 3-in-1 Transformer, a payment foundation model that integrates sequence, tabular, and graph representations for payment risk detection. The model contains approximately 7B parameters, with approximately 1.7B activated per task route. Antom 3-in-1 Transformer is pretrained to learn reusable behavioral and relational representations, primarily on Ant International's internal payment data. In a cross-business transfer experiment, pretraining improves the target business metric by 34.5% over the same architecture trained from scratch. With only 25% of the training labels, the pretrained model outperforms the full-label scratch baseline in Average Precision (AP) and Recall@0.5% on different merchant domains. In a four-month online experiment on Ant International's billion-scale payment platform, the model reduced the overall loss rate by 37.88% relative to XGB-Online.
hf.title_ja: Antom 3-in-1 Transformer: 決済基盤モデル
hf.summary_ja: シーケンス、表、グラフ表現を統合し、少数のラベルで高精度な決済リスク検知を実現。

hf.title: Embo-Harness: Towards Understanding Frontier-Model-as-Policy Harness
hf.abstract: Frontier multimodal models exhibit extraordinary generalization in generating robot actions from observations and instructions, enabling a new paradigm in which they serve directly as policies within closed-loop robotic harnesses. However, the design principles of such harnesses, and the capabilities underlying their strong performance, remain unclear. We present Embo-Harness, a framework for systematically studying frontier-model-as-policy harnesses. We investigate four components of the robotic agentic loop, namely, prompting, planning, action execution, and tool use, and distill six empirical findings into a practical recipe. This recipe prioritizes interfaces that exploit the model's native visual reasoning and tool-use capabilities over handcrafted plans, skills, or action priors, and identifies effective choices for action representation, chunking, reasoning effort, visual observations, short multi-action sequences, and policy refinement. On RoboLab-120, Embo-Harness achieves an 83.3\% success rate, outperforming the strongest reported baseline by 26.2 percentage points. It also succeeds in 15 of 20 zero-shot trials across four real-world manipulation tasks. Beyond performance, controlled interventions indicate that the studied model depends more strongly on accurate spatial target estimation than on explicit low-level joint or trajectory generation. These results provide both a practical recipe for building strong frontier-model-as-policy harnesses and a clearer account of the capabilities that drive their performance.
hf.title_ja: Embo-Harness: フロンティアモデルを方策とするハーネスの理解に向けて
hf.summary_ja: マルチモーダルモデルをロボット方策として活用する際の最適な設計指針を体系化。

hf.title: Don't Sleep, Keep Watch: Proactive Perception for Computer-Use Agents
hf.abstract: Computer-use agents (CUAs) built on vision-language models are increasingly entrusted with long-horizon tasks in live desktop, web, and mobile environments, where the screen keeps changing on its own. However, current CUAs lack real-time situational awareness: they perceive the environment through discrete snapshots, and the substantial inference latency of VLMs, compounded by highly dynamic interfaces, opens a perception-action gap in which the observed state frequently becomes stale before the corresponding action is executed. To bridge this gap, we present NightWatch, a plug-and-play framework that endows any CUA with continuous, temporally grounded perception without changing the agent's model, prompt, or action space. NightWatch couples the VLM agent with NightWatch-0.8B, a lightweight System-1 model that performs streaming monitoring of the interface state and keeps the agent synchronized with the evolving environment at low computational cost and latency, thereby grounding each decision in the current state rather than an outdated snapshot and reducing both stale actions and idle waiting while preserving task success. Experiments on desktop and dynamic web environments (OSWorld-Verified and DynaCU-Bench) show that NightWatch, driven by a watcher of only 0.8B parameters, reduces non-reasoning wall-clock time by 33% and wasted time by 53% on OSWorld while keeping task success on par, raises success on DynaCU-Bench from 39.5% to 44.2% with the large VLM agent, and is more efficient than passive-watching baselines such as AOI and PUSV under the same screenshot-only input, as well as a System-1 decision model more than 30times its size. Overall, NightWatch demonstrates that the timing of perception is as critical as its content, marking a step toward agents that maintain continuous awareness of their environment rather than perceiving it turn by turn.
hf.title_ja: Don't Sleep, Keep Watch: コンピュータ利用エージェントのための能動的知覚
hf.summary_ja: 推論遅延による知覚の乖離を防ぎ、動的な画面変化に追従する連続的な知覚機能を付加。

hf.title: Lazy Agents Answer Against Their Own Beliefs: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Beliefs Teaches Them to Act on What They Believe
hf.abstract: AI agents working on long tasks often commit to an answer before they have enough evidence, a behavior called laziness. In our evaluations, they frequently commit even while their stated belief still names several possible answers. An outcome reward at the end of the episode scores only the final answer, so it cannot teach the agent when to commit, because a lucky guess receives the same reward as an answer backed by evidence. During training, however, the simulator can compute the exact posterior over the answer at every step and tell whether the evidence is already enough. We propose Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Beliefs (RLVB), which rewards the agent for taking further steps while this posterior still allows several answers and for committing once the evidence is sufficient. The reward needs no judge, critic or reward model, and it never reads the belief line the agent writes before each action. We also introduce Pro Worlds, a benchmark of visual puzzles where the agent views a large world through a small window. We evaluate three vision-language models on three benchmarks, two of which are never seen in training. RLVB improves the base model in all nine settings, by 17.1% on average. Under the outcome reward, GRPO and PPO fall below the base model on average. RLVB also outperforms PPO with a process reward from an LLM judge by 9.3% on average while using 1.6 times fewer GPU-hours. The trained agent answers with sufficient evidence in 51%, 12% and 74% of the episodes on the three benchmarks, against 8%, 0.4% and 36% for the base model. Its accuracy gain therefore comes from answering more often at high levels of evidence. The belief line shows how the agent reaches this evidence: it acts on its own belief. It commits at only 0.1 to 2.2% of the turns at which the evidence is insufficient and its line still names several answers, against 3 to 68% for the base model.
hf.title_ja: 怠惰なエージェントは信念に反して答える：検証可能な信念を持つRLによる改善

hf.title: cmHC: Balancing Stream Mixing in Hyper-Connections via Geometric Contraction
hf.abstract: Manifold-constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC) extends residual connections to multiple streams and stabilizes residual propagation by constraining stream-mixing residual matrices to the Birkhoff polytope, the set of doubly stochastic matrices. In this work, we investigate how to effectively mix residual streams within the Birkhoff polytope. We reveal a mixing trade-off: when under-mixed residual matrices stay close to the vertices of the Birkhoff polytope, hyper-connections will degenerate into a set of nearly independent streams; when over-mixed residual matrices are concentrated around the uniform barycenter of the polytope, streams will become less distinguishable from each other. We theoretically validate our findings by bounding the cumulative residual mixing, stream difference and gradient difference of mixing coefficients across layers. Motivated by these findings, we propose Contraction for Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections (cmHC), an exact doubly stochastic method which geometrically contracts the Birkhoff polytope toward its interior. This contraction mitigates under-mixing by forcing the residual matrices to explore deeper into the polytope, with a provable stream mixing bound and no new parameterization. Moreover, we apply a moderate contraction at the shallow layers to prevent over-mixing, enabling stable gradient propagation on extremely large-scale model pretraining. Extensive experiments across dense and mixture-of-experts models at various parameter scales demonstrate the effectiveness and scalability of cmHC. We also develop fused operators for cmHC on Ascend NPUs, reducing hyper-connection execution latency by up to 44.8%.
hf.title_ja: cmHC: 幾何学的収縮によるハイパーコネクションのストリーム混合の調整
hf.summary_ja: 多層残差結合の混合度合いを制御し、情報の縮退を防いでモデルの学習効率を向上させる。

hf.title: Rewirable Circuits in Transformers with Loom Attention
hf.abstract: We propose loom attention, which allows a Transformer to dynamically rewire its circuits at every token by interweaving a head's vertical attention over the outputs of earlier heads (to obtain its query, key and value) with its horizontal attention over tokens. We instantiate vertical attention efficiently with normalized and gated linear attention over a per-token matrix memory, which stores the compressed head outputs and serves as a second residual stream. This yields LoomFormer, a dual-stream architecture that splits control and content between the vector and matrix streams. Across model sizes and training token budgets in language modeling and downstream tasks, LoomFormer matches Transformers trained with over 3x compute and recent residual-stream baselines (HC/mHC, MUDDFormer, AttnRes) trained with ~1.7-2.8x. For example, trained on the same 300B tokens with only 2% extra FLOPs, LoomPythia-2.8B achieves ~1.6x the average downstream gain of mHC-Pythia-2.8B over Pythia-2.8B, and matches (0-shot) or surpasses (5-shot) Pythia-12B. Code is available at https://github.com/Caiyun-AI/LoomFormer

hf.title: Sage-Med: Scaling Medical Multimodal Intelligence
hf.abstract: Establishing effective scaling laws for medical multimodal large language models (MLLMs) remains a persistent and fundamental challenge. Our systematic evaluation shows that existing medical MLLMs tend to underperform frontier general-purpose MLLMs across a range of medical tasks, while scaling model size primarily improves text capabilities rather than multimodal perception, and enabling reasoning modes fails to close this visual gap. To investigate how medical multimodal intelligence scales in practice, we introduce Sage-Med-Preview, a 35B-parameter medical multimodal model with 3B activated parameters, built by combining stage-specific curation over 322.7 million candidate records with a progressive training curriculum spanning medical pretraining, staged supervised fine-tuning, and adaptive reinforcement learning. Across this curriculum, progressive supervised refinement and adaptive reinforcement learning yield consistent stage-wise gains, substantially advancing both specialized visual understanding and medical language capabilities. Evaluated against 77 competing models across 238 clinical tasks spanning 61 public and 13 private multi-center benchmarks in more than 40 modalities, Sage-Med-Preview achieves an average score of 58.26% on the 31 public multimodal benchmarks. It outperforms the state-of-the-art open-source medical model Hulu-Med-235B-A22B at 50.99% and the general scientific model Intern-S2-Preview at 52.24%, and approaches the advanced proprietary model GPT-6.2-Sol across multiple tasks such as comprehensive multimodal understanding, report generation, and visual grounding. Although substantial challenges remain in complex medical reasoning and multi-step clinical workflows, this report provides empirical evidence, actionable data and training recipes, and a rigorous benchmark toward scalable clinical multimodal intelligence.

hf.summary_ja: 322.7Mの記録で訓練した35Bモデルにより、医療特有の知覚と推論能力を向上。

hf.title: Mixture-of-Loops Transformer
hf.abstract: Looped Transformers boost expressivity by reusing shared layers across loops, yet at the cost of efficiency. Pushing their expressivity-efficiency frontier requires rethinking the core mechanism connecting adjacent loops: What should be passed as a Transformer loops? We introduce Mixture-of-Loops Transformer (MoLT), whose Mixture-of-Loops Attention (MoLA) uses keys and values (KV) as memory for selective reuse across depths and loops. Under loop residual, MoLT-R retains the residual stream and reads local KV across loops for expressivity. Under loop KV, MoLT-KV instead restarts from embeddings and reads current-loop local KV with preceding-loop memory KV at earlier positions for efficiency. MoLT-KV eliminates same-position cross-loop dependence and, paired with loop forcing for parallel training, unlocks single-traversal Mixture-of-Loops (MoL) decoding beyond the training loop horizon. To balance efficiency and quality, we introduce U-shaped MoLT (U-MoLT), which separates memory construction from prediction readout and skips unused decoder traversals without changing predictions. In 400B-token pretraining, U-MoLT outperforms OLMo3 across 700M/1.5B dense and 3B MoE models, achieving 1.7x validation cross-entropy (CE) token efficiency at 700M while improving 3B MoE 10-domain perplexity by 0.75 and 10-task accuracy by 2.1 percentage points. In 100B-token continued pretraining of Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base, our U-MoLT adaptation lowers CE on all 11 domains over the matched baseline with 1.4x mean token efficiency. At inference, U-MoLT with MoL-Hybrid-2 matches non-looped OLMo3 latency at 996.6 vs. 1,000.6 ms on S-size (~113M) models. Code is available at https://github.com/hustvl/MoLT

hf.summary_ja: KVキャッシュを層・ループ間で選択的に再利用し、表現力と計算効率の限界を打破する。

hf.title: ACAP: Asynchronous Coding Agents for Efficient Robot Control
hf.abstract: Coding agents can construct and revise robot behavior during execution, but using one agent for the whole robot can delay otherwise independent work. We introduce Asynchronous Coding Agents as Policy (ACAP), an asynchronous framework that organizes one robot as a team of persistent agents. Each member reasons and acts for a configurable control group, such as an arm with its gripper or the torso and chassis, enabling asynchronous reasoning and execution. However, different robot components often have physical dependencies that require coordination. To address this challenge, ACAP introduces a hyper-agent that assigns tasks, coordinates dependencies, and dynamically allocates control between the lead and member agents. This allows independent work to progress concurrently while supporting tightly coupled manipulation when necessary. Across 72 real-world rollouts covering 25 task/platform settings, ACAP reduces task-balanced time cost by 28.2% compared with a single-agent Direct Policy, with improvements across Fully Parallel, Parallel-Sequential, and Collaborative tasks. Across all eight Collaborative settings, ACAP also achieves lower mean time cost than Fixed Delegation, where only member agents can control their assigned groups. An additional 90-rollout study shows lower mean 30-minute-capped time cost than Direct on all six tasks. We further demonstrate mobile manipulation using the same member interface for chassis and torso control. We present the framework and a real-world rollout dataset containing observations, generated programs, actions, and feedback to support research on how coding agents reason and act in the physical world.
hf.title_ja: ACAP: 効率的なロボット制御のための非同期コーディングエージェント
hf.summary_ja: ロボット部位ごとに独立したエージェントを割り当て、依存関係を調整しつつ並列実行。

hf.title: 3AGameFactory-Motion: Agentic Rigging and Reliable Complex Motion Generation for Diverse 3D Assets
hf.abstract: Animating arbitrary 3D assets from instructions requires both structural inference and motion control, yet existing motion benchmarks mostly cover conventional human or animal skeletons with simple instructions. We introduce DivDynBench, which evaluates rigging and motion generation across six morphology categories, with instructions requiring multi-phase part coordination and explicit timing, angle, repetition, and trajectory constraints. With large language models, we systematically compare three common paradigms: specialized motion generation, video generation followed by motion recovery, and direct agent-driven generation. We analyze their control capabilities, cross-morphology adaptability, and generation costs. Guided by this comparison, we propose an Agentic Motion Framework in which an agent writes compact parametric skeleton and motion programs, and a deterministic executor performs rigging, kinematic solving, and geometric correction. Compact parameter control reduces generation overhead and improves rigging reliability and motion-control accuracy, providing practical guidance for deploying complex 3D motion generation.
hf.title_ja: 3AGameFactory-Motion: 多様な3D資産のためのエージェントによるリギングと動作生成
hf.summary_ja: 複雑な制約を持つ多様な形態の3Dモデルに対し、リギングと協調動作の生成を評価。

hf.title: Non-penetrating World Models
hf.abstract: We study a new problem of preventing object penetration in interactive video world models. To understand how existing models handle this, we introduce NoPeBench, a benchmark that evaluates how world models respond to physical obstacles. Our evaluation reveals that none of the open-source models can reliably prevent such failures. Surprisingly, however, these models already encode the information needed to predict such violations. We find that the hidden states of diffusion transformers (DiTs) can predict whether a candidate action will penetrate an obstacle. Building on this, we introduce NoPeWorld, a lightweight framework that detects and prevents penetration. Specifically, we train a small prediction head on top of a frozen DiT's hidden states to read out if a candidate action is safe or not. Unsafe actions are then replaced with safe ones that best preserve the original intent. Despite its simplicity, NoPeWorld substantially reduces the physical violation rate, averaged over six video world models, from 74% to 16%. Remarkably, our method shows zero-shot generalization to open-domain imagery, third-person viewpoints, and moving obstacles. We publicly release our code, the NoPeBench benchmark, and model weights. Project Page: https://nopeworld.github.io .
hf.title_ja: 非貫通型ワールドモデル
hf.summary_ja: ビデオ生成での物体貫通を検知・防止する軽量フレームワークとベンチマークを提案。

hf.title: Let the Fixer Decide: Training a Code Localizer from the Fixer's Likelihood
hf.abstract: Code localizers are usually trained to predict the files a reference patch edits, but the code a fixer needs to read is not the same as the code it changes. We propose Fixer-Guided Localization (FGL): the localizer proposes several localizations, a frozen fixer scores each by how likely it makes a verified patch, and the localizer is trained on these scores with weighted supervised fine-tuning, without running tests and without reinforcement learning. We build the full pipeline on Gemma 4 E4B for the Kaggle Gemma-4 Developer Agent competition, from 1,629 test-verified Kimi K3 trajectories. The FGL target helps the fixer find the bug as often as the teacher's localization while using 27.5% less code. On the development set, one EM round moves the agent in the expected direction compared with a matched control: more tasks reach a patch (53 vs. 46), fewer tasks get stuck reading files that do not exist (43 vs. 54), and more tasks are solved (8 vs. 6). Training also changes how the agent works: trained agents explore about three times more than the base model and write far fewer wrong patches, and the single agent solves up to 11 of 78 tasks, against 8 for the base model. An analysis of 13 evaluation runs identifies what limits a 4B agent under an 8-minute budget (time, repetition loops and edit quality) and gives practical lessons for training small coding agents. All data, code and adapters are publicly available.

hf.title: DyLoMo-DiT: Dynamic Looped Mixture-of-Experts Diffusion Transformers
hf.abstract: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) scale model capacity by increasing both parameter count and computation. Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) variants expand parameter capacity while keeping per-token computation roughly fixed, but still require substantial parameter storage. In this paper, we propose Dynamic Looped MoE DiT (DyLoMo-DiT), which reuses parameters rather than adding them: a weight-shared loop repeatedly applies the middle layers, while sparse experts allocate parameter capacity across tokens. This design deepens the network without adding parameters, freeing the parameter budget for other uses, such as more experts or more distinct layers. It also allocates compute dynamically, varying the number of passes across noise levels. Experiments show that DyLoMo-DiT makes more effective use of parameter and compute budgets, with further gains from assigning more passes to low-noise steps. On ImageNet 256times256, DyLoMo-DiT reduces FID by 11-24% relative to DiT and 36-56% relative to DiT-MoE at matched parameter and compute budgets. For text-to-image generation, a scaled DyLoMo-DiT achieves a higher GenEval score than FLUX.1 (0.714 vs. 0.673), with less than one tenth of its active parameters (1.05B vs. 12B).

hf.title: A Glimpse of Training VLMs as Foundation Models for Robotic Manipulation
hf.abstract: Recently, GPT-6 Astra demonstrates strong generalization in robot control, yet limited disclosure of its training leaves open how such capabilities can be reproduced. We introduce nanoAstra, an approach to training vision-language models (VLMs) for generalizable manipulation that combines semantic action modeling with capability-preserving supervised fine-tuning (CP-SFT). nanoAstra represents robot behavior as semantic steps composed of reusable, parameterized action primitives, guided by explicit progress descriptions. Meanwhile, CP-SFT uses an explicit robot-specific system prompt to constrain manipulation outputs to a structured action space, aiming to focus adaptation on robot-specific contexts and promote specialization while minimizing interference with broader pretrained capabilities. With this formulation, we train nanoAstra on more than 5,000 hours of robot data together with general VQA data. On RoboTwin 2.0's randomized benchmark, nanoAstra-9B achieves a 17.8% zero-shot success rate, substantially outperforming advanced VLA and WAM baselines as well as similarly sized VLMs. With inference faster than the corresponding motion execution on a single H20 GPU, our model supports action-chunk-like streaming execution that overlaps inference with motion, reducing the robot's idle time from 35.0% to 6.9%.

hf.title: VibeVideoAgent: Closing the Perceptual Loop for Code-Driven Video Generation
hf.abstract: Code-driven video generation asks a coding agent to write and run rendering programs. This gives exact control over typography, data visualizations, synchronized audio, and multi-shot scenes, and it leaves an editable project behind. A program that exits cleanly can still render overlapping labels, a camera aimed away from its subject, broken object interactions, or narration that drifts out of sync, and none of these raise a runtime error. Feeding rendered frames and audio back into the coding session bloats its long-horizon context, while critiquing only the finished full-resolution render turns early design mistakes into costly rewrites. We introduce VibeVideoAgent, a training-free framework that lets coding agents inspect their drafts throughout production. Multimodal perception runs in short-lived contexts kept apart from the coder and returns compact, grounded Findings. Seven primitives operate on a unified multi-clock representation of assets and drafts: they explore media from coarse to fine, verify quoted requirements with evidence from every required modality, compare a draft with a reference or an earlier revision on separate clocks, and measure stream signals locally. A lightweight staged protocol has the agent test its riskiest decision on a minimal preview first. On all 239 VibeVideoBench tasks, with matched agent runtimes and a fixed perception model, VibeVideoAgent improves holistic audiovisual quality (L3) for Claude Opus 5.5 (4.03 -> 4.43, while L2 rubric compliance rises from 98.87% to 99.35%), GPT-6 Astra (4.03 -> 4.27), and Claude Sonnet 5.5 (3.97 -> 4.10), with the largest gains in audio-visual synchronization (up to +0.56). Controlled ablations show that each component contributes, and trajectory audits show that the granularity of code edits governs the trade-off between rubric adherence and perceptual quality.

hf.title: WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce
hf.abstract: We present WeMM-Ecom, a family of multimodal large language models that deliver frontier e-commerce capabilities while achieving state-of-the-art general-purpose performance at their respective scales. The family spans five sizes, from a 0.8B dense model to a 35B mixture-of-experts model with 3B active parameters. Our training pipeline begins with two-stage continued pre-training that progressively raises the proportion of e-commerce data within a diverse multimodal data mixture, followed by hybrid-thinking post-training that combines on-policy distillation and reinforcement learning to support both non-thinking and thinking modes. For evaluation, we construct a comprehensive suite of 28 e-commerce benchmarks (23 in-house and five open-source) covering eight business scenarios and complement it with 64 public general-purpose benchmarks. On the e-commerce suite, WeMM-Ecom-35B-A3B surpasses substantially larger open-source flagship models, including Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, HY4, and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. On the general-purpose suite, every WeMM-Ecom model surpasses its similarly sized Qwen3.5 counterpart, with the lightweight variants (e.g., WeMM-Ecom-2B) showing clear advantages over leading lightweight models such as Qwen3.5-2B, MiniCPM-V-4.7-1B, and LFM3-VL-2B. Beyond benchmarks, WeMM-Ecom now powers hundreds of production use cases in WeChat, including catalog management, multimodal product search, and livestream commerce, serving billion-scale requests per day. We publicly release all model weights and detail our data curation, training recipe, and benchmark construction to facilitate future work on domain-specialized multimodal models. We have released the model weights and code to facilitate future research at https://github.com/Tencent/WeMM-Ecom.

hf.title: Self-Evolving Evaluation Environments for Computer-Use Agents
hf.abstract: Computer-use agents (CUAs) are rapidly improving, yet their evaluation remains largely static. Existing benchmarks provide a strong foundation, but fixed difficulty ceilings, limited feature coverage, and coarse aggregate scores progressively weaken their discriminative and diagnostic value. We introduce CUA-SEE, a closed-loop evaluation environment that co-evolves tasks and executable verifiers from rollout evidence. It disentangles three objectives: benchmark evolution expands evaluation scope through cohort-calibrated difficulty and coverage growth; diagnostic evolution increases resolution through agent-conditional capability-boundary probes; and verifier evolution improves precision by translating changing requirements into state-grounded checkpoints with adversarial validation. Across multiple agents, applications, and rounds, CUA-SEE generates challenging, measurable tasks while preserving process-level evidence. Our results position adaptive evaluation as a scalable counterpart to self-evolving agents, continuously tracking what agents can do, where their boundaries lie, and how reliably progress is measured.

hf.title: Stable Gated DeltaNet-2: Understanding and Mitigating Recurrent State Instability
hf.abstract: Linear attention offers an efficient solution for long-sequence modeling via linear complexity and fixed-size recurrent states. Gated DeltaNet-2 (GDN-2) introduces independent channel-wise control over erasure and writing, enhancing state-update expressiveness and in-context retrieval, yet it suffers from training failures during long-context training. We trace these failures to the asymmetry between reading and modification directions during erasure, which yields non-normal erase operators whose directional gains accumulate across tokens, triggering exponential state growth even without new writes. To resolve this, we propose , employing symmetric erasure to ensure non-expansive state propagation and decay-regulated residual writing to preserve writing flexibility. Theoretically, we establish an O(T) upper bound on recurrent state growth while retaining chunkwise parallel computation. Experiments on ~1.6B parameter models show that achieves stable training alongside improved long-context retrieval. Compared to GDN-2, it boosts the 128K average RULER score by 6.80 points in the recurrent setting and average accuracy across nine downstream tasks by 0.62 points in the hybrid setting.

hf.title: Clover-35B-A3B-Preview Technical Report
hf.abstract: We introduce Clover-35B-A3B-Preview (Clover), a mixture-of-experts diffusion language model with 35 billion total parameters and 3 billion activated parameters, supporting thinking-mode generation. Clover adapts Gated Delta Networks to block diffusion by combining recurrent memory of previously generated context with bidirectional softmax attention inside the current block. Historical memory readout competes with current-block tokens in a shared softmax, with learnable block-size calibration and a separate, zero-initialized right-context convolution branch. Clover leads the seven evaluated agent metrics, including 73.6 on SWE-bench Verified and 51.7 on Terminal-Bench 2.1. On internal agent workloads, it reaches a reported generation speed of 680 tokens/s using one NVIDIA GB300 GPU at BF16 precision and batch size one. We organize the evaluation around model quality, drafting and verification costs, and deployment under constrained memory. We also describe a decision-model variant that generates answers to related questions in one denoising pass. On an internal set of 500 groups, joint prediction raises question accuracy from 90.37% to 93.88% and all-correct group accuracy from 65.4% to 77.0%.

hf.title: Improving and Expanding Video Editing Capabilities Without Videos
hf.abstract: Image editing models can follow a wide range of instructions, but video editing models still lag behind, limited in part by the difficulty of collecting paired source and edited videos. Is it possible to transfer advanced image editing capabilities to video editors without new paired videos? We introduce Image-to-Video Transfer (I2VT), which improves pretrained video editors and expands them to new editing tasks using an image editor. It enables efficient post-training with no architectural changes and no new videos, using only individual images. Our key idea is to let the video editor role-play as an image editor: it edits an image as a one-frame video, with the image editor guiding the video editor's predictions at each denoising step. Although the video editor sees only single images during training, at test time it applies the improved and expanded capabilities to whole video clips while preserving temporal consistency. To push the boundaries of video editing, we introduce OpenVE++, an extension of OpenVE-Bench that adds four new editing tasks useful for video production, including action changes, expression changes, body movements, and scene relighting. Our experiments across three different video editors show that I2VT improves existing editing capabilities and expands them to new tasks, and our models achieve state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance on both OpenVE-Bench and OpenVE++.

hf.title: PyRUA-Dex: Learning Programmatic Policies for Dexterous Bimanual Manipulation with Coding Agents
hf.abstract: Learning for dexterous manipulation is limited by the scarcity of high-quality demonstrations: retargeting from human video is imprecise, teleoperation gives no force feedback to the operator, and exoskeleton-based collection is hard to scale up. We present PyRUA-Dex, a framework that enables coding agents to develop dexterous manipulation through programmatic policy, without the need of demonstrations. The programmatic policy is developed in two stages: during exploration, multiple agents explore in parallel for task skills and ways to compose them, and a distilling agent condenses the successful attempts into a task library and one program. During refinement, this program is improved through randomized layouts for enhanced robustness and execution efficiency. In simulated environments, PyRUA-Dex achieves SOTA on Bench2Dex with a score of 72.9 and reaches 81.0% success on DexJoCo under full randomization, ahead of every trained policy on both benchmarks. In real world experiments on a bimanual platform with two 22-DoF hands, PyRUA-Dex learns to play piano, write calligraphy, and other tasks efficiently: learning a new piece from sheet music takes as little as 30 minutes. These results suggest that PyRUA-Dex is an effective framework for developing dexterous manipulation policies with coding agents in the absence of high quality dexterous manipulation demonstrations.

hf.title: Innata-0: A Native Embodied World System with Model-Agent Co-Design
hf.abstract: The physical world is open-ended, dynamic, and partially observable. While foundation models have advanced embodied intelligence, standalone models struggle with long-horizon execution, and simply integrating models with agents may lead to inconsistencies between planning and physical control. To support reliable and adaptive behaviors in the physical world, we introduce Innata-0, a native embodied world system. Innata-0 jointly designs an embodied world-action model and an agent to combine their complementary strengths. The model, Innata-0-WAM, adopts a tri-tower Mixture-of-Transformers architecture that integrates understanding, prediction, and action generation. The agent, Innata-0-Agent, coordinates long-horizon execution through memory, verification, and recovery. A co-design protocol is further proposed to align model training with agent execution and leverage validated experiences to support subsequent adaptation and model improvement. Extensive evaluations demonstrate strong embodied capabilities across understanding, world prediction, and robotic manipulation. Innata-0 represents our first step toward physical intelligence, and we see it as the beginning of a much longer journey.

hf.title: Learning Video Foresight Reasoning from Unlabeled Videos via On-Policy Self-Distillation
hf.abstract: Video foresight reasoning requires vision-language models to anticipate future events or next actions from currently observed videos. Existing methods fit future captions, rationales, or full visual states, but face two limitations. First, they rely on annotations or external large models for supervision, limiting scalability. We address this with an on-policy self-distillation framework that turns past-future video pairs into a natural self-supervised signal without extra annotations or LLM supervision. Second, they treat the whole future clip as equally valuable, although most of it is irrelevant context information. We address this by defining a foresight score, from which we obtain a contrastive privilege advantage that drives the model to learn the most valuable future information. Since the score is intractable, we optimize a tractable lower-bound surrogate that interpolates this advantage, computed between the true and a random reference future, with a teacher-student distillation advantage; together, they amplify decision-relevant content information and suppress irrelevant context information. We call the resulting framework Future-OPSD. On open-ended prediction and closed-ended planning, Future-OPSD improves base models by up to 14.2 and 15.9 points without compromising general video understanding. Code will be available at https://jingchensun.github.io/future-opsd/

hf.title: ViDecide: Teaching Video Diffusion Models to Reason and Plan Step by Step
hf.abstract: Current leading video generation models can synthesize highly realistic videos, while still frequently violating physical and logical constraints in multi-step reasoning and planning, even after training with large-scale reasoning data or existing diffusion RL methods. We attribute these failures to the conventional video training paradigm, which treats a solution as a fixed-length clip rather than a chain of decisions. We present ViDecide, a decision-centric framework that trains video diffusion models to predict state transitions causally and decide when to stop, with a decision-focused training schedule. We further propose Corrective Fine-tuning (CFT), which corrects failed decisions by mapping their noise to the model's own successful continuations, achieving stable improvement without policy-gradient optimization. Across abstract games, planning tasks, and a new benchmark of multi-step robot planning, ViDecide achieves an average strict success rate of 83.8%, far above 23.3% for standard fine-tuning and 67.8% for the strongest prior method, and generalizes to larger puzzles and unseen layouts. Our framework therefore unlocks greater potential for video generation models as reliable reasoners and planners in the visual world. Project page: https://kevin-thu.github.io/ViDecide.

hf.title: S-Mind: Internalizing Multi-View Geometry for Spatial Intelligence
hf.abstract: Spatial intelligence, the ability to reason about 3D space from visual observations, becomes essential as multimodal large language models (MLLMs) move into the physical world. Beyond perceiving each view, it rests on two cornerstones of human cognition: fusing multiple views into one coherent 3D scene and mentally transforming that scene to new viewpoints as reasoning unfolds. Yet our spatial probes reveal that MLLMs largely lack both capabilities, even after spatial fine-tuning. We therefore present S-Mind, which internalizes multi-view geometry within the MLLM through a compact set of spatial tokens. It supervises these tokens to hold the fused 3D scene and re-emits them to re-express this scene from every viewpoint the reasoning adopts. Across four spatial benchmarks, S-Mind improves its Qwen3.5 backbones by up to 22.26 points and surpasses frontier general models such as GPT-6-Astra (+0.45), Kimi-K3.1-Pro (+1.97), and GLM-5.3-Flash (+7.80) in average accuracy. Moreover, the same probes confirm that it acquires both capabilities, reaching fusion and transformation accuracies of 65.11% and 82.17%, against at most 16.02% and 37.28% for the baselines. At inference, S-Mind also runs about 100x faster than a tool-based agent on the same backbone. Instilled through these spatial tokens during training, spatial capability becomes intrinsic to the backbone and persists even when the tokens are withheld, offering a promising path toward spatial intelligence in MLLMs.

hf.title: PartAgent: Agentic 3D Part Segmentation via Expert Integration and Closed-Loop Refinement
hf.abstract: Segmenting a 3D object into semantically meaningful parts requires joint reasoning about geometric structure and semantic context. Pretrained 3D experts provide spatially grounded region proposals, while 2D experts provide semantic cues for identifying object parts. The challenge is to integrate these complementary capabilities into a framework that can both produce meaningful part segmentations and progressively refine them. We present PartAgent, a training-free agentic framework for 3D part segmentation built upon two complementary modules: (i) Structural-Semantic Expert Integration combines regions predicted by the 3D expert with multiview semantic evidence from the 2D expert through image-to-surface correspondences, constructing compositional part partitions at multiple granularities. (ii) Observation-Driven Closed-Loop Partition Refinement observes the current partition and its supporting evidence to select targeted inspection, evidence repair, composition, or reselection actions. It verifies proposed changes and uses the updated state and action outcomes to guide subsequent decisions. On PartObjaverse-Tiny-WT, PartAgent achieves 68.41 mIoU, outperforming the strongest competing method by 8.53 points. Across 3DCoMPaT200, PartNeXt, PartNetE, and PartObjaverse-Tiny, PartAgent achieves the highest mIoU on each dataset, averaging 69.36 across the four datasets, 7.28 points above the highest mean among competing methods.

hf.title: AutoPILOT: A Visual Agent Harness for Real-Time Gameplay
hf.abstract: Multimodal foundation models can play video games well when the game waits for them, but often fail when it keeps running. We find that much of this gap lies in the harness, which decides what the model sees, what it remembers, and how its outputs become actions over time. Existing harnesses such as VISTA improve the first two, yet turn each model call into at most one action, so the agent acts only as often as its model thinks. We introduce AutoPILOT, which changes the third: in each model call, the model can send a primitive action, start an open-loop macro, or write a closed-loop controller that keeps playing from the screen without further model calls until it hands control back. To evaluate agents in real-time games, we build AFK-Bench, 120 diverse browser games grouped by how they respond to inaction and playable in real time or with the clock paused. With GPT-6.1 Sol under the same budgets, AutoPILOT reaches 68.6% real-time success against 38.3% for VISTA, and on GameWorld it keeps 80.0% in real time while VISTA drops from 84.1% to 42.9%. Its gains hold across models, and it reaches VISTA's final success rate at a fifth of its API cost. Our results suggest that how a harness turns model outputs into actions over time is a central yet underexplored part of agent design, and we hope AutoPILOT and AFK-Bench will serve as a foundation for agents in a world that does not wait.

labs.title: Depth Pro 2: Sharp and Temporally Consistent Metric Monocular Depth
labs.summary: We present Depth Pro 2, an approach to estimating dense metric depth for images and video at full resolution. By analyzing prior methods for monocular depth estimation, we find that they commonly trade off temporal consistency and boundary sharpness: multi-frame methods favor consistency, single-frame methods favor sharpness. To overcome this trade-off, we train a single, scalable network that processes both images and video and predicts depth maps at native resolution. labs.summary: Latent 3D representations have significantly expanded the capabilities of modern shape modeling, enabling compact encoding of 3D scenes and supporting powerful 3D generative models.
